sections.skill: Recognize speculation and common investment frauds and protect yourself

questions.domain: Investing, Brokerage Accounts, and Investment Products
questions.prompt: A message promises "a guaranteed 20% return every month with no risk." What is the best response?

choices.text: Invest a small amount to test it before investing more
Treat it as a likely scam and do not invest
Invest quickly before the offer ends tonight
Ask the sender for a written guarantee first

questions.correct_answer: Treat it as a likely scam and do not invest
questions.intro: Red flags of investment fraud include guaranteed high returns with little or no risk, pressure to act quickly, unregistered sellers, and complicated or secret strategies. Legitimate investments carry risk, and no one can guarantee high returns.
questions.feedback: Guaranteed high returns with no risk is the classic sign of fraud.
questions.topic: Speculation, crypto assets, and investment fraud

misconceptions.A: Scams often pay small early returns to build trust
misconceptions.D: A guarantee from a scammer means nothing

sources: SEC Investor.gov: Red flags of investment fraud include promises of guaranteed high returns, pressure to act quickly, and unregistered sellers; Ponzi schemes pay earlier investors with new investors' money. (https://www.investor.gov/protect-your-investments/fraud/types-fraud)

SEC Investor.gov: Crypto asset investments are highly risky and volatile, and are not FDIC insured or SIPC protected in the same way as deposits and securities at member firms. (https://www.investor.gov/additional-resources/spotlight/crypto-assets)

questions.domain: Investing, Brokerage Accounts, and Investment Products
questions.prompt: In a Ponzi scheme, where does the money paid to early investors come from?

choices.text: From newer investors' money
From real profits on the investments
From government insurance
From interest earned at a bank

questions.intro: A Ponzi scheme pays existing investors with money from new investors instead of real profits. It collapses when new money slows, and most investors lose money.
questions.feedback: Ponzi schemes recycle new investors' money to pay earlier investors.
questions.topic: Speculation, crypto assets, and investment fraud

misconceptions.D: Believes the returns are real interest

questions.domain: Investing, Brokerage Accounts, and Investment Products
questions.prompt: A crypto token rises 300% in a month after heavy social media promotion. Which statement is MOST accurate?

choices.text: It is guaranteed to keep rising
It is protected by FDIC insurance up to $250,000 per owner
It is a safe place for an emergency fund
It is highly speculative and could fall just as fast

questions.correct_answer: It is highly speculative and could fall just as fast
questions.intro: Speculation is buying something mainly hoping its price rises quickly, often without regard to its underlying value. Crypto assets are highly volatile, are not FDIC insured, and have been targets of fraud and "pump-and-dump" schemes.
questions.feedback: Rapid hype-driven gains are speculative and can reverse quickly.
questions.topic: Speculation, crypto assets, and investment fraud

FINRA BrokerCheck or the SEC's Investment Adviser search

questions.prompt: Pumpers buy a little-known stock, hype it online, and sell when others rush in. What is this called?

choices.text: Dollar-cost averaging scheme
A pump-and-dump scheme
Diversification
Rebalancing

questions.intro: In a pump-and-dump, promoters spread false or misleading hype to push up a price, then sell their shares at the high price, leaving others with losses.
questions.feedback: Promoters "pump" the price, then "dump" their shares.

questions.domain: Investing, Brokerage Accounts, and Investment Products
questions.prompt: Insured savings pay about 4% a year, and stocks have historically averaged under 10% a year with large swings. A "no-risk 10% per month" offer is…

choices.text: far beyond any realistic, risk-free return
reasonable for a new, fast-growing company
the same as a savings account
normal for index funds

questions.correct_answer: far beyond any realistic, risk-free return
questions.intro: Knowing typical returns helps spot offers that are too good to be true. No legitimate investment offers high returns with no risk.
questions.feedback: 10% per month (over 200% a year) with no risk is unrealistic.

questions.prompt: Which payment method do investment scammers often ask for because it is hard to reverse?

choices.text: A credit card with dispute rights
A check to a registered broker-dealer
An ACH transfer to your own brokerage account
Crypto transfers, wires, or gift cards

questions.feedback: Irreversible payment methods are a scam warning sign.

questions.prompt: Who controls access to crypto held in a "self-custody" wallet?

choices.text: The FDIC
Whoever has the private keys or recovery phrase
The crypto exchange that sold the coins
The wallet app's customer service team

questions.correct_answer: Whoever has the private keys or recovery phrase
questions.intro: Crypto wallets are controlled by private keys or recovery phrases. Anyone who gets them can take the assets, and lost keys can mean lost assets.
questions.feedback: Keys control the wallet; never share a recovery phrase.

Pump-and-dump
Phishing
